description: PowerShell cmdlet to retrieve firewall rules from Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security.
prerequisites: Administrative privileges for remote queries or full rule visibility

flags.purpose: Retrieves firewall rules by their display name using wildcard matching.
flags.security_use_case: Find rules allowing RDP, SMB, or other sensitive services that attackers may enable for lateral movement.
flags.threat_detected: Unauthorized enabling of Remote Desktop or file sharing ports by malware or attackers.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Wildcards may return many rules.
flags.safe_followup: Use Set-NetFirewallRule to disable suspicious rules after verification.

flags.purpose: Filters firewall rules based on whether they are enabled or disabled.
flags.security_use_case: Audit all currently active firewall rules that impact live traffic flow.
flags.threat_detected: Malicious rules enabled to allow backdoor communication or data exfiltration.
flags.safe_followup: Compare with baseline firewall policy for deviations.

flags.purpose: Filters rules based on traffic direction (Inbound or Outbound).
flags.security_use_case: Review inbound rules that allow unsolicited connections into the system.
flags.threat_detected: Backdoor ports opened to accept incoming attacker connections.

flags.purpose: Filters rules that explicitly allow traffic through the firewall.
flags.security_use_case: Identify all allow rules which could permit risky or unauthorized communication.
flags.threat_detected: Firewall rules allowing command-and-control or exfiltration channels.
flags.safe_followup: Validate necessity of each allow rule against policy.

flags.purpose: Filters rules applied to specific network profiles (Domain, Private, Public).
flags.security_use_case: Detect rules active on Public profile which may expose the system on untrusted networks.
flags.threat_detected: Rules mistakenly enabled on Public networks increasing attack surface.
flags.safe_followup: Restrict risky rules to Domain profile only if appropriate.

powerful_combinations.command: Get-NetFirewallRule -Enabled True -Direction Inbound -Action Allow | Get-NetFirewallPortFilter | Select-Object Name,Protocol,LocalPort
powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Shows exactly which inbound ports are currently open and allowed through the firewall.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detecting unauthorized open ports used by malware, backdoors, or lateral movement tools.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Quickly finds rules related to high-risk remote access and file transfer services.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Identifying services attackers typically enable for persistence or data exfiltration.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Reveals whether rules were created locally or pushed via Group Policy.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detecting locally added firewall rules that bypass organizational security policy.
